purpose: Visual operating map for LoopTool as the bounded local execution/evidence bridge inside the GPT-Knowledge engineering workflow. This map explains when to use it, when not to use it, how command/result transport works, how it composes historical Memory retrieval for existing plans/decisions/disagreements, and what evidence it can and cannot prove.
authority_rule: Current GPT-Knowledge routing, current Letterblack0306/tools source, active local workspace identity, returned AGENT RESULT evidence, current Memory/BirdEye evidence and live runtime/rendered behavior outrank this projection. LoopTool is transport/evidence, not the historical-memory owner, investigation owner or acceptance authority.

nodes.title: Deterministic local execution bridge
nodes.summary: Use LoopTool for local testing, debugging, repository inspection, validation, reproduction and bounded command execution. The reasoning agent decides what evidence is required; LoopTool transports one selected local action and returns evidence.

nodes.title: Not the reasoning agent
nodes.summary: LoopTool must not interpret the whole investigation, invent the next fix, or become a blind command/fix loop. Agents reason; the bridge executes and returns evidence.

nodes.title: Keep authorities separate
nodes.summary: GPT-Knowledge owns reusable method/routing; Memory owns canonical historical retrieval; GitHub owns remote repo truth; active workspace owns local file/revision truth; BirdEye owns governed local evidence; LoopTool owns command transport/evidence return; live runtime/UI owns behavioral acceptance.

nodes.title: Route through GPT-Knowledge
nodes.summary: Start from 000_START_HERE.md and knowledge-index.json, then load only the smallest task-relevant method/skills. Project/feature work must route through project-feature-implementation-plan.md before implementation-oriented LoopTool use.

nodes.title: Establish exact identity
nodes.summary: Before consequential execution establish repository, project, branch/revision, working directory and runtime identity as applicable. Do not execute against an assumed workspace.

nodes.title: Recover prior plan / decision when relevant
nodes.summary: When the user asks what was planned, decided, rejected, corrected, tried or implemented before, scope the question to the exact project/workspace/feature first and retrieve historical evidence before reinventing the direction.

nodes.title: One question + observable
nodes.summary: Define one bounded question, the authoritative observable, a falsifier and the acceptance condition before issuing the command. The command should answer that question rather than explore randomly.

nodes.title: Testing / debugging / inspection
nodes.summary: Use when deterministic local evidence is required: reproduce a failure, inspect repo/runtime state, run focused tests, validate a fix, execute a bounded maintenance command, or collect stdout/stderr/exit-code/runtime evidence.

nodes.title: Existing plan / decision / disagreement recall
nodes.summary: LoopTool can compose GPT-Knowledge project mapping, BirdEye local identity and Memory historical retrieval to recover prior plans, decisions, corrections, rejected approaches and implementation evidence with provenance. LoopTool transports the bounded retrieval; Memory remains the historical owner.

nodes.title: Historical recall + evidence guide
nodes.summary: The LoopTool project carries historical-recall-evidence-guide-2026-08-26.md covering Memory/Cline retrieval, provenance, bounded context, disagreement/correction chains, historical_evidence_non_truth classification and current-truth reconciliation.

nodes.title: LoopTool + Memory recall skill contract
nodes.summary: GPT-Knowledge now includes project-engineering/looptool-memory-recall-skill.md. The skill tells reasoning agents when to use the seven Memory MCP capabilities with LoopTool, preserves exact provenance, uses runtime > workspace > session > project docs > historical evidence > derived memory > inference authority, and explicitly forbids mandatory recall, stale-history promotion and Memory-owned reasoning workflows.

nodes.title: Choose the owning historical source
nodes.summary: Use the imported GPT/ChatGPT archive for broad conversation history, Cline session history for Cline/tool/runtime-session evidence, and Memory exact/semantic/hybrid retrieval as the canonical historical interface. Do not assume one source contains all history.

nodes.title: Scope before ranking
nodes.summary: Bind retrieval to project/workspace/repository/feature/session/time anchors before semantic or keyword ranking. A high-scoring mixed-project session is not authoritative merely because it contains matching terms.

nodes.title: Preserve rejected and superseded history
nodes.summary: Retrieve disagreement, correction, rejection and supersession context instead of hiding old statements. Historical evidence can remain searchable even when stale or wrong; retrieval does not promote it to current truth.

nodes.title: Use conversation graph context
nodes.summary: ChatGPT archive conversations may branch. Do not infer chronology from SQLite row adjacency. When correction history matters, use conversation/node relationships and the relevant active branch.

nodes.title: History proposes; current evidence resolves truth
nodes.summary: Historical plans and decisions answer what happened before and why. Present-state claims about branch, files, wiring, runtime health or current authority must be reconciled against GitHub, BirdEye/current workspace or live runtime evidence before being stated as truth.

nodes.title: Explicit LoopTool execution
nodes.summary: Use when the user explicitly asks for LoopTool / Workspace Launcher Loop / local execution, or when the routed workflow selects LoopTool as the direct local evidence path.

nodes.title: No local evidence requirement
nodes.summary: Do not activate LoopTool for general coding questions, architecture discussion, documentation-only review, theoretical explanation, or code suggestions when no deterministic local execution evidence is required.

nodes.title: Never investigation owner
nodes.summary: Do not use it as a run-everything mechanism, a substitute for repository reasoning, a blind retry/fix loop, or a way to claim acceptance from a successful command alone.

nodes.title: Do not duplicate BirdEye blindly
nodes.summary: When BirdEye is the governed evidence layer, use its workspace/revision/search/inspect/run path when appropriate. Do not run the same command through BirdEye and LoopTool without an explicit cross-validation reason.

nodes.title: AGENT COMMAND envelope
nodes.summary: Execution request format: === AGENT COMMAND START ===, WORKING DIRECTORY: <absolute project path>, COMMAND: <PowerShell command>, === AGENT COMMAND END ===. Working directory is part of the execution contract.

nodes.title: Execute one bounded action
nodes.summary: Run the smallest action that can answer the defined question. Avoid broad mutation, destructive cleanup, or unrelated commands unless explicitly justified by the routed investigation.

nodes.title: AGENT RESULT evidence
nodes.summary: The documented result channel returns evidence shaped as AGENT RESULT with command status/hash, working directory, command, exit code and runtime output such as stdout/stderr. Treat the current implementation as something to verify, not assume from documentation.

nodes.title: Classify only observed layer
nodes.summary: Command emitted is not command executed. Exit code 0 is not feature acceptance. A focused test pass is not end-to-end proof. Historical retrieval rank is not authority. Classify evidence only at the layer actually observed.

nodes.title: Separate transport/runtime failures
nodes.summary: Distinguish command failure from bridge delivery failure, session loss, dependency/configuration block, stale test/fixture, harness failure and product/runtime failure before changing code.

nodes.title: Workspace containment
nodes.summary: Verify the command targets the intended active workspace and remains inside allowed workspace boundaries. Local evidence is only meaningful when workspace/revision identity is known.

nodes.title: Capability owner != exposed adapter scope
nodes.summary: 2026-08-26 LBE workspace evidence: canonical LBE already owns governed workspace.delete, while the exposed filesystem deletion MCP adapter was scoped to C:/Users/prave and therefore was not used against C:/Agents-Memory-Tool-v6-integration. Four generated directories remained; protected .agent/.cline state and lbe-tui/ were untouched. This is an adapter-scope boundary, not proof of a missing delete capability.

nodes.title: Live runtime closes behavior claims
nodes.summary: When the claim is behavioral or user-visible, continue from LoopTool evidence to the required live runtime/rendered UI acceptance. LoopTool output alone does not prove behavior it did not observe.

nodes.title: Verify implementation drift
nodes.summary: Protocol documentation and Letterblack0306/tools may drift. Before implementation-specific claims, inspect current source/runtime and revalidate parser, readiness, duplicate suppression, timeout/cancellation and result-return behavior as relevant.
